headline: Google kills Manifest V2 for Chrome, impacting ad blockers
summary: Google is phasing out Manifest V2 extensions in Chrome versions 150 and 151, a move that will break many popular ad blockers.
details: Google is proceeding with the discontinuation of Manifest V2 extensions in its Chrome browser, a significant shift that will render many existing ad blockers ineffective. This transition, which has been in progress for years, is now entering its final phase with versions 150 and 151.

The move to Manifest V3 imposes more stringent requirements, aiming to enhance user and app safety online. Users who rely on current ad-blocking tools will likely need to migrate to compliant alternatives.

Under Manifest V3, extensions will lose the ability to intercept data dynamically. While new Manifest V3-compliant ad blockers are available on the Chrome Web Store, they often utilize predefined lists and may not be as effective as their predecessors.

For users seeking a less restrictive experience, alternative browsers like Mozilla's Firefox offer continued support for Manifest V2 alongside V3. Alternatively, VPN services with ad-blocking capabilities, such as NordVPN, can provide a workaround.

headline_marked: Meta rolls out [[AI tools for Facebook]] with photo editing and chatbots
headline: Meta rolls out AI tools for Facebook with photo editing and chatbots
summary: Facebook users can now ask an AI chatbot questions and edit photos using new AI-powered features, leveraging Meta's Muse Spark technology for unique insights.
details: Meta has launched a suite of new AI tools directly within Facebook, aiming to enhance user experience through conversational AI and advanced photo editing capabilities. These features are designed to offer more personalized and context-aware interactions.

The core of the update is the AI Mode chatbot, which answers user questions by pulling data from across Facebook's ecosystem, including Groups and Reels. Meta claims this will provide 'real perspectives and experience' beyond generic search results, powered by its Muse Spark technology.

Beyond conversational AI, the update introduces robust photo-editing tools. Users can expect new collage cutout templates for altering photos from their camera roll and novel transition effects for creating 'smooth, stylized video montages' with a single tap.

Additionally, new AI-powered photo presets allow users to alter elements like clothing, hair, and accessories within images. Meta specifically pitches this for sports fans, enabling them to 'virtually wear a team jersey' to show their support.

These new AI features are rolling out immediately to mobile Facebook users. While a web version is not confirmed, Meta's focus appears to be on enhancing the mobile experience where camera roll access is native.
